summary: The G and 2D shifts with power are laser heating, not strain or doping. From 0.5 to 5 mW, G moves from 1581.27 to 1579.50 cm-1 and 2D from 2669.52 to 2664.39 cm-1, with G and 2D broadening and the Si line fixed. Trust only the 0.5 mW spectrum for strain/doping, and treat even that as a possibly slightly heated upper bound. It indicates roughly unstrained, lightly doped, low-defect single-layer graphene. The 2 and 5 mW positions must not be used. At 5 mW, a 2D of ~2664 cm-1 would look like ~0.2% tensile strain, which would be a false result.

observations.finding: G and 2D red-shift and broaden monotonically with laser power: thermal softening, not sample-intrinsic strain or doping.
Spectrometer drift is excluded and there is no laser damage.
observations.evidence: Si 520 line fitted at 520.86, 520.90, 520.91 cm-1 (fixed to ~0.05). G height per mW 1522, 1499, 1503; Si height per mW 2336, 2255, 2255 (linear, same integration time). D band undetected, D/G < ~0.02 (0.5 mW) and ~0.01 (5 mW), at the noise limit.

observations.finding: The shift ratio ΔG:Δ2D is 1:2.9 and matches neither the doping nor the strain vector cleanly. Heating mimics strain (similar ratio), so the ratio cannot be used as a strain/doping fingerprint.
observations.evidence: ΔG = -1.77 cm-1, Δ2D = -5.13 cm-1 (0.5→5 mW); ratio 2.9. Literature (from memory): strain ~2.2, hole doping ~0.7.
observations.source: Mohiuddin et al., PRB 79, 205433 (2009); Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012), ωG–ω2D correlation figure

observations.finding: The temperature rise between 0.5 and 5 mW is of order 100-150 K, from the literature thermal coefficients (rough estimate).
observations.evidence: -1.77/-0.016 ≈ 110 K from G; -5.13/-0.03 ≈ 150 K from 2D. Coefficients quoted from memory.
observations.source: Calizo et al., Nano Lett. 7, 2645 (2007) (values to be verified)

observations.finding: The lowest-power spectrum indicates single-layer graphene with low doping and little strain and a low defect density.
observations.evidence: At 0.5 mW: narrow single-Lorentzian 2D (32 cm-1), I2D/IG height ~3, G FWHM 13.7 cm-1, G 1581.3 cm-1, 2D 2669.5 cm-1. The 2D/G area ratio is nearly constant (7.0→6.6), so doping is roughly stable across powers. D is undetected.
observations.source: Reference undoped/unstrained G ~1581.6 cm-1 from Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012) (recalled, not checked)

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: none (not resolvable; 0.5 mW spectrum close to unstrained reference, heating dominates the power-dependent shifts)

properties.name: temperature_rise_0.5_to_5mW_K
properties.source: Calizo et al., Nano Lett. 7, 2645 (2007) (coefficients from memory)

caveats: Even 0.5 mW may be locally warm: the shifts per mW are still large (about -0.4 cm-1/mW for G and -2 cm-1/mW for 2D). 2D is nonlinear in power, so extrapolating to zero power is unreliable.
Si reads 520.9 cm-1 against the nominal ~520.5 cm-1, so a calibration offset of about +0.4 cm-1 may exist. It matters for strain below ~0.05%.

The baseline is not proportional to power and changes shape (about 50-380 counts at 0.5 mW, 300-1100 at 2 mW, 1500-3600 at 5 mW). It is probably a substrate/optics background or offset. It does not affect the peak positions.
Photodesorption of adsorbates at high power could also shift and broaden G, and cannot be excluded.
Strain and doping cannot be rigorously separated from one laser energy, one spot and heated spectra.
Cited coefficients and reference positions are from memory and not verified against the papers.
questions_for_user: Is the graphene supported on SiO2 everywhere under the spot, or suspended or rippled? This sets the heating.
What are the spot size, integration time and number of accumulations? I need them to convert power to power density and to confirm the three spectra are equivalent.
In what order were the spectra taken, and was the spot exposed to 5 mW before the 0.5 mW spectrum? The order matters for photodesorption and for any hysteresis.
Can you take a power series at 0.1, 0.2 and 0.5 mW and extrapolate to zero power?
Was the spectrometer calibrated against a Si or neon line before these measurements?
Do you have maps or other spots, and a second laser wavelength, to check homogeneity and the 2D dispersion?
citations: Calizo et al., Nano Lett. 7, 2645 (2007) (temperature dependence of graphene G and 2D)
Mohiuddin et al., Phys. Rev. B 79, 205433 (2009) (uniaxial strain in graphene by Raman)
Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024 (2012) (ωG–ω2D correlation, separating strain from doping)
limits: Does not give a quantitative strain or doping value, because heating contaminates every spectrum and only three powers were measured.
Gives no information on spatial homogeneity from a single spot.
The temperature estimate relies on literature coefficients that were recalled from memory and not verified, and the sample's own coefficients may differ.
The D-band limit is set by noise and baseline, so the data cannot exclude a very low defect density below D/G ~0.01-0.02.
Does not distinguish thermal shifts from photodesorption or other laser-induced doping changes.
